### rustfs/rustfs (rustfs)

### [`v1.0.6`](https://redirect.github.com/rustfs/rustfs/releases/tag/1.0.6): RustFS 1.0.6

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/rustfs/rustfs/compare/1.0.5...1.0.6)

#### What's Changed

- Keep legacy MRF work queued after physical repair and add MRF management on the release branch ([#​9391](https://redirect.github.com/rustfs/rustfs/issues/9391), [#​9399](https://redirect.github.com/rustfs/rustfs/issues/9399)).
- Backport scanner usage convergence and retire obsolete scanner work without clearing responsibility for pending work ([#​9397](https://redirect.github.com/rustfs/rustfs/issues/9397)).
- Update the Rust 1.100 lint fixes and use a larger macOS release runner.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/compare/1.0.5...1.0.6>

### [`v1.0.5`](https://redirect.github.com/rustfs/rustfs/releases/tag/1.0.5): RustFS 1.0.5

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/rustfs/rustfs/compare/1.0.4...1.0.5)

#### Upgrade notes

- Complete the upgrade from 1.0.4 on every node before adding or removing pools, or retrying a decommission operation.
- While 1.0.4 and 1.0.5 nodes coexist, DELETE requests handled by new nodes may temporarily return HTTP 503. Retry them after all nodes are upgraded. The compatibility check verified existing data integrity and DELETE recovery after the upgrade.

<!-- rustfs-generated-release-notes: managed; remove this marker before manual edits -->

#### Known issue on macOS

The macOS archive can display an extra `1.0.5-preview.1` line because both tags identify the same source commit. This affects version text and may affect update notifications. The archive source, startup, Console and S3 read/write/delete checks were verified. This minor issue is tracked for 1.0.6; the new candidate pipeline explicitly stamps the final product version.
